stemMd: In skeletal muscle contraction, which statement describes the sliding-filament mechanism?

options.label: A
options.textMd: ATP has no role in the cross-bridge cycle.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The sarcomere lengthens whenever force is generated.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Actin filaments are fully digested during each contraction.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Actin and myosin filaments slide past one another without substantially shortening themselves.

explanationMd: Myosin heads interact cyclically with actin, moving the filaments relative to one another. The overlap increases as a sarcomere shortens, while the individual filament lengths remain approximately constant. ATP powers the cycle and allows myosin to detach from actin.

distractorRationale.c: Contraction does not require destruction of the filaments.
distractorRationale.b: Sarcomeres can shorten while generating force.
distractorRationale.a: ATP binding and hydrolysis are essential to normal cross-bridge cycling.
